subject: Next steps: Demo scheduling & rotating time slots

From: Laura Mitchell <laura@acmeanalytics.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-20T09:02:00-07:00
Subject: Next steps: Demo scheduling & rotating time slots

Vivek — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap from our side and a request to align calendars for the next demo / technical deep dive:  

Recap (high level):
- Primary use case: inference at scale for our: query-side ranking + customer-facing generation in low-latency paths.
- Top concerns: predictable p99 latency, ROI on reserved vs. burst capacity, and data residency for EU customers.
- Technical ask for the next session: a 45–60 minute session that covers architecture (KV cache, batching), deployment options (dedicated vs. private), and an initial cost/throughput projection.

Calendar constraints and stakeholders:
- We have three stakeholders who must attend at least once: Laura (SF/PST), Tom (London/GMT+1), and Mei (Singapore/HKT).  
- Ideally we do a rotating schedule so each region sees a session that falls in their normal working hours.

Can you propose a rotation approach (e.g., week-by-week rotating windows) and a few concrete time options next week? We also prefer a recurring slot (every other week) so the engineers can plan.

Thanks — happy to make any times work if you suggest something sensible.

Laura Mitchell
Head of ML Platforms
Acme Analytics
laura@acmeanalytics.com
+1 (415) 555-0198

P.S. Tom (cc) will help coordinate scheduling on the London side.

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Laura Mitchell <laura@acmeanalytics.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-20T11:14:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Next steps: Demo scheduling & rotating time slots

Laura — great to meet you both today. Appreciate the clear priorities. I sketched a pragmatic rotating schedule that tends to keep the primary region in normal business hours each week while letting us keep a single recurring meeting on your calendar. Proposed approach below + concrete slots next week.

Rotation proposal (round-trip model):
- Week A (US-friendly): 90-minute window at 09:00 PDT / 12:00 EDT — covers SF and East Coast observers.
- Week B (EU-friendly): 60-minute window at 15:00 BST / 16:00 CEST — convenient for London and mainland Europe.
- Week C (APAC-friendly): 60-minute window at 10:00 SGT / 11:00 HKT — covers Singapore/Hong Kong attendees.

We recommend a 3-week rotation instead of alternating every week so participants see at least one session that lands in their normal day each month while minimizing churn. We can make this recurring every other week with a 3-week skip pattern if that’s easier for calendar tooling.

Concrete slots for next week (pick one — I’ll send the invite and rotate afterward):
- Option 1 (US-first): Tue 2027-06-22, 09:00–10:30 PDT (SF-friendly)
- Option 2 (EU-first): Wed 2027-06-23, 15:00–16:00 BST (London-friendly)
- Option 3 (APAC-first): Thu 2027-06-24, 10:00–11:00 SGT (Singapore-friendly)

Suggested agenda (attached: Demo_Agenda_roundtrip.pdf):
- 0–10m: quick re-intro and goals
- 10–30m: architecture walk-through (runtime, KV cache, routing/fallback)
- 30–50m: demo of a request path + latency breakdowns
- 50–60m: Q&A and next steps (contract/timeline follow-up)

Attachments: Demo_Agenda_roundtrip.pdf (agenda + participant checklist). I’ll also attach a one-page Rotation_playbook_v1.docx that outlines how we handle invites and recurring rotation.

Links: HubSpot deal (ACME-4521) for reference: https://hubspot.company/deals/ACME-4521 — I’ll log the chosen slot there and create a calendar event: https://calendar.google.com/event?eid=roundtrip-proposal

If you prefer, I can also create a short Calendly poll for the three options. Once we lock the first session we’ll mark the rotation pattern and automate follow-up invites.

Thanks — Vivek
Sr. Solutions Lead | Redwood Inference
vivek@redwood.com | +1 (650) 555-0312

- Attendees we recommend on our side: Vivek (solutions), Ben (solutions engineering), Monica (CS lead).
- For the technical deep dive please confirm whether you want us to bring a short data sample or use a synthetic example. If you can share a sanitized sample ahead of time (S3 link or upload to the HubSpot deal), Ben can adapt the demo to match your latency distribution.

My pick for the first show: Option 1 (Tue 6/22 09:00 PDT). It gives the longest overlap for internal SEs to attend and we can record for the EU/APAC stakeholders who can rotate in for later weeks.
